data.text:
The Long-Overdue Awakening of a Nation 🇵🇭

In the face of rampant corruption and systemic abuse, thousands gathered at the People Power Monument in EDSA and filled Luneta Park in protest—marking not only the 53rd anniversary of Martial Law under the late dictator Ferdinand Marcos Sr., but also etching a defining moment in our collective memory.

For our September cover, Metroscene Mag stands as a platform for the young, empowered, and creative. We capture this undeniable truth: the Filipino people are watching. This was no ordinary march. It was defiance in motion, a resounding declaration that the nation has had enough.

Since our inception, this is what we’ve stood for—amplifying stories of resistance, of courage, of voices demanding to be heard. This issue brings the people’s struggle to the forefront: a call for justice and a warning to those in power. A reminder that the Filipino spirit is restless, awake, and vigilant.

Metroscene Mag marches with the movement — POWER TO THE PEOPLE! 

📖 Read the full cover story: https://t.co/fTVpbCw3jG

#MetrosceneMagSeptember2025

Moving Cover Editor: @cloydegodoy
Creative Director, Art Director, and  Editor-in-Chief: @wadupels

data.text:
DDS, MASTERMINDS NG MENDIOLA RIOTS?

Politiko PH reports:

"An Iskooper said authorities are investigating the possible involvement of lawyer Ferdinand Topacio, former Executive Secretary Vic Rodriguez, former Manila City Administrator Bernie Ang, and ex-Manila congressman Harry Angping in the riot along Mendiola, which left 129 police officers and 76 civilians injured.

Topacio currently serves as PDP-Laban’s spokesperson in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. Rodriguez unsuccessfully ran for senator under the Duterte-led slate, while Ang heads the party’s National Capital Region chapter.

Angping has also courted controversy in the past. He was reportedly arrested by Thai police in November 2022 for allegedly harassing a hotel staff member at the Marriott Marquis Queen’s Hotel in Bangkok — a scandal that was said to have prompted the resignation of his wife, Zenaida, as chief of the Presidential Management Staff.

One group caught up in the unrest was the Kalayaan Kontra Korapsyon (KKK) Movement. Its spokesperson, Aldrin Cabajes, claimed in a Facebook post that their protest had been “hijacked” by Duterte Diehard Supporters (DDS).

“When we went to Mendiola, the riot started. The people who provoked it were not from our groups. Kids and teens suddenly appeared, riding an L300 van. Allegedly they were paid by some people, allegedly mga DDS,” Cabajes wrote.

He added that chants of “Duterte, Duterte” dominated the rally, forcing the original organizers to withdraw.

#Mendiola

data.text:
Several parents of minors who were arrested during the September 21 rally in Mendiola trooped to the Manila Police District (MPD) headquarters to check on the condition of their children.

According to Oscar Oida’s Monday report on “24 Oras,” the parents said they had no idea of their children’s well-being after violence broke out along Recto Avenue in Manila during the September 21 protest.

A total of 216 persons were arrested by the police, of whom 89 are minors. They are currently being processed by authorities.

Read more: https://t.co/ctArmTcgaC
